title: Mini-protocols: tool transactionality & session resume (notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note to capture compact, implementable mini-protocols for two interlocking capabilities we keep iterating on: (1) transactional tool-calls in streaming responses (idempotent/atomic tool invocation boundaries), and (2) session resume semantics for interrupted/paused streams plus SDK ergonomics for both.

Why this doc exists (problem space):
- Hosted API is increasingly used for long-running multi-tool transactions (search -> api call -> db write -> summarise) where partial generation is streamed to clients.
- Current streaming semantics let clients see interim tokens, but there is no clear, low-friction contract for:
  - marking "tool call start / tool call end" boundaries so downstream systems can safely execute side effects without double-execution,
  - resuming a stream after a network interruption while preserving correctness and minimal duplication,
  - giving SDKs ergonomic primitives that reduce app developer surface area around retries and fallbacks.
- Goal: propose minimal wire/SDK patterns that allow safe tool transactionality and pragmatic resume/backpressure handling without massive server-side state overhead.

Constraints / principles:
- Minimal server-side sticky state per session (we want to scale).
- Backwards-compatible: should be optional and interoperable with existing streaming endpoints.
- Client-first ergonomics: SDK should make correct usage easy; advanced users can opt into details.
- Visibility: every critical event should be observable (audit logs, traces) to diagnose double-invoke and resume anomalies.
- Reasonable eventual consistency for non-critical side-effects; strict atomicity required only when user opts-in.

High-level design summary (two pieces):
1) Transaction tags + idempotency tokens embedded in stream frames
   - The model stream includes lightweight control frames that mark transaction lifecycle: TRANSACTION_START, TRANSACTION_COMMIT, TRANSACTION_ABORT.
   - Each transaction has a short client-visible transaction_id (UUID v4 truncated to 12 chars) and optional idempotency_token if client wants server to persist a short mapping for retry dedupe.
   - Tool-adaptor processes (or gateway components) consume these control frames and use transaction_id + idempotency_token to decide whether to execute or skip side-effects.

2) Resume offsets + provenance checkpoints
   - Streams emit periodic CHECKPOINT frames with: sequence_offset (token index or chunk index), last_committed_transaction_id, and a cryptographic short provenance (HMAC over prior context + checkpoint counter).
   - On reconnect, client sends ResumeRequest {session_id, resume_offset, last_known_checkpoint_proof}. Server validates proof and either resumes from offset or returns a compact reconciliation summary: list of committed transaction_ids since checkpoint.

Wire framing (stream frame types) - minimal set we propose:
- TEXT (continuation token text)
- CONTROL: {type: one of [TRANSACTION_START, TRANSACTION_COMMIT, TRANSACTION_ABORT, CHECKPOINT, META]} (embedded as small JSON payload)
- BINARY_ATTACHMENT (for tool payloads or trace logs)

Example stream snippet (human readable):
- TEXT: "Searching for flights..."
- CONTROL: {"type":"TRANSACTION_START","transaction_id":"t-3f9a1b","idempotency_token":"cli-55b"}
- TEXT: "Calling flightSearch API with params: ..."
- BINARY_ATTACHMENT: {"tool_payload_ref":"s3://tmp/req-123"}
- CONTROL: {"type":"TRANSACTION_COMMIT","transaction_id":"t-3f9a1b","status":"success","tool_result_ref":"gs://res/xyz"}
- CONTROL: {"type":"CHECKPOINT","offset":421,"last_committed":"t-3f9a1b","proof":"hmac:..."}

Operational semantics (server + adapters):
- TRANSACTION_START: server records a short-lived in-memory entry mapping transaction_id -> resume-window-start; if idempotency_token present, write a small dedupe entry to a fast KV for N minutes (configurable) so duplicate reconnects won't re-trigger heavy side-effects.
- TRANSACTION_COMMIT/ABORT: transitions are emitted by the model runtime once the generated tokens indicate closure; adapters must only complete side-effects on COMMIT.
- CHECKPOINT: indicates a safe resume point; server can garbage-collect older transient state up to last checkpoint retention window.
- If a client reconnects with a resume request and server has checkpoint and dedupe entries, it will answer OK and resume streaming from the requested offset; if the server cannot reconstruct, it will return a reconciliation hint: list of committed transaction_ids and small metadata so client can reconcile (e.g., skip local UI actions).

SDK ergonomics (JS + Python high level):
- Expose two high-level models: "optimistic-tool" and "durable-tool".
  - optimistic-tool: lowest friction, SDK executes local on COMMIT events but does not guarantee dedupe across long disconnects. Good for non-critical side-effects (notifications, ephemeral webhooks).
  - durable-tool: uses idempotency_token and waits for server-ack (CHECKPOINT including last_committed == transaction_id with proof) before surface as completed to app. SDK provides automatic retry helper that will re-attach and reconcile history if net break occurs.
- API surface (JS pseudo):
  - const s = client.createSession({resume: true});
  - s.on('toolCommit', (txn, result) => { /* durable: persists or invoke once */ });
  - s.resume({sessionId, offset}) -> Promise<reconciledEvents>
- Default SDK behavior: durable-tool for built-in Redwood connectors (db, billing) and optimistic-tool for user-provided webhooks unless user opts into durable semantics.

Backpressure and partial writes:
- Keep control frames small and prioritized: CHECKPOINT frames are control-critical and should be sent in separate transport packets when possible.
- On client slow consumption, server will try to buffer up to a small window (configurable) but should send CHECKPOINT earlier and allow client to request flow-control window size change.
- If buffer pressure causes loss of in-memory mapping for transactions, server will mark those transactions as low-fidelity: still emit COMMIT frames but with a reconciliation hint that clients must consult reconciliation API to determine side-effect status.

Failure modes and how to surface them:
- Duplicate-execution risk if client does not resume and decides to re-run same user request from scratch. Mitigation: SDK-generated idempotency_token persisted in local storage or app layer, plus server-side dedupe TTL.
- Stale checkpoint: if proof validation fails on resume, server returns 'REQUIRES_RECONCILE' with a list of committed transaction IDs and timestamps. SDK should surface a reconcile prompt to developer (or auto-skip for optimistic tools).
- Partial tool payload lost: store tool_payload_refs for a retention TTL and expose admin audit view to re-run or inspect.

Telemetry / observability requirements:
- Emit events for TRANSACTION_START/COMMIT/ABORT and resume attempts with resolution (OK/REQUIRE_RECONCILE/NO_STATE).
- Dashboard views: outstanding incomplete transactions per session, percent of resumed sessions requiring reconciliation, distribution of checkpoint intervals (ms).

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide:
- Checkpoint frequency vs perf: more frequent CHECKPOINTs = easier resume, but more overhead and trace volume. Default: every 5s or 512 tokens, whichever comes first (configurable per tenant).
- Server state retention TTLs: dedupe idempotency entries 10m by default for optimistic mode, 24h for durable connectors? Need SRE input.
- Proofing scheme: HMAC vs signed opaque proof. HMAC requires shared secret rotated; signing requires key infra. Start with HMAC short proof and evolve.
- UX for partial local side-effects: should SDK auto-compensate (eg. issue compensating delete) when relay shows duplicate? This gets into app semantics; recommend leaving compensation policy to app.

Next actions / short-term roadmap (concrete):
- Product: decide default checkpoint cadence and dedupe TTL (owner: Laura). Due: 2025-03-07.
- Eng (runtime): implement CONTROL frame emitter hooks and proof HMAC stub in streaming runtime (owner: Marco). Spike 2-week.
- Eng (gateway/adaptors): implement small KV dedupe store abstraction and opt-in durable-tool path. (owner: Jin).
- SDK: prototype resume API and durable-tool helper in JS (owner: Daniel). Reachable demo by 2025-04-01.
- Security: review HMAC proof approach for replay risks (owner: security team).

Notes / rough TODOs in this doc (work-in-progress):
- Add sample SDK code snippets for Python + Go.
- Produce compliance matrix: which persisted proofs are PII-free? We must ensure tool payload_refs are redacted in public logs.
- Flesh out migration plan so existing streaming clients continue to work if they ignore CONTROL frames.

Quick FAQs (anticipated):
Q: If I never use durable-tool, do I need to change anything?
A: No. Existing stream-only patterns still work. Durable features are opt-in.

Q: Who pays for extra storage for dedupe?
A: Host tenants (Redwood) will manage the short TTL store; enterprise customers can request longer retention under contract.

Q: Can tool commits be reordered on resume?
A: The wire contract preserves transaction_id ordering in the stream; resume will provide committed-ids list in order. Reordering across independent sessions is possible but orthogonal.

End notes:
This remains a working draft; aim is to keep framing small and implementable so we can iterate with a customer pilot (SE-led) rather than designing an all-encompassing solution. Add feedback below or ping in #product-hosted-api.
